A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same study, with matching authors, research questions, methods, and substantial shared content. All 30 pages of v1 and 40 pages of v2, including appendices and figures, support comparison. Internal reporting inconsistencies in v2 are noted below.

before.justification: v1 reports original imputation and prediction experiments on real and semi-synthetic regression datasets, including repeated-split results, correlations, regression slopes, and computation times.

after.justification: v2 reports original results for the retained experimental framework and adds MNAR experiments, missing-rate sensitivity, feature-importance analyses, and shuffled-indicator controls.

M1.justification: The four imputation procedures, MLP, SAINT, XGBoost, native missing-value handling, and true-indicator input construction remain unchanged. The added missingness mechanisms and shuffled indicators serve experimental scenarios and controls; they do not revise a proposed prediction method.

E1.justification: v2 extends the MCAR evaluation to probit self-censoring MNAR data and adds a 70% MCAR condition. The plotted dataset roster changes from 20 to 19: california, fifa, isolet, and year panels disappear, while abalone, delays_zurich_transport, and yprop_4_1 appear. Table 1 inconsistently retains fifa instead of delays_zurich_transport, leaving that roster detail unresolved.

E2.justification: The main benchmark retains the same four imputers, three predictors, and two native-handling alternatives. Appendix I.2 adds shuffled-indicator pipelines as control comparators for assessing indicator benefits. Newly cited missingness-aware architectures and encodings are not added to the evaluated benchmark.

E3.justification: New protocols include calibrated probit self-masking, evaluation at 70% missingness, per-sample shuffling of indicator columns, and permutation importance computed separately on observed and imputed subsets for each dataset's two most important features. Section 4.2 also revises the stated centering of imputation R2 by dropping pooling across missing rates. The existing 80/10/10 splits, sample caps, preprocessing, and hyperparameter settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendices G-I add missing-rate sensitivity, observed-versus-imputed feature importance, analysis of indicator gains versus imputation accuracy, and shuffled-indicator controls. Section 4.4 and Appendix L test whether the findings extend to MNAR missingness. These substantially expand the questions tested beyond v1's retained real-versus-linear-outcome analyses.

E5.justification: v1 already reports ten repeated splits and Nemenyi comparisons. v2 substantially extends inference to the central effect estimates: Figure 4 introduces one-sided coefficient t-tests with Bonferroni correction, Section 4.3 adds Wilcoxon tests of positive effects across datasets, and Appendix H tests feature-importance differences. Significance markers also appear in supplementary slope plots. The stated repetition count remains ten.

E6.justification: Main and supplementary results are revised, and substantial MNAR, sensitivity, and indicator-control findings are added. In the matched Bike_Sharing_Demand example at 50% missingness, Figure 3 changes MLP/MLP-with-indicator slopes from 0.24/0.03 to 0.23/-0.01 and correlations from 0.66/0.30 to 0.64/-0.13. New MNAR results report negative average effects for SAINT and XGBoost without indicators. Aggregate revisions also involve changed dataset coverage and therefore do not establish same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: Appendix L.1 adds a formal probit self-censoring definition and Proposition L.1, with a proof deriving a bias parameter for a target missing rate under Gaussian assumptions. This is an auxiliary theoretical addition supporting the new experiments. Proposition C.1 retains its mathematical content, with variables renamed and explanatory prose expanded.

C1.justification: The central claims about diminishing returns, expressive predictors, indicator benefits under MCAR, and linear versus real outcomes remain. The introduction strengthens v1's conjecture of smaller benefits beyond MCAR into a claim that MNAR experiments confirm smaller benefits, although the conclusion retains cautious wording.

C2.justification: v2 interprets the shuffled-indicator results as evidence that feature-specific missingness information explains indicator benefits, rather than regularization or missing-value counts alone. It adds explanations for mean imputation's MNAR performance and discusses variation among MAR/MNAR mechanisms. The limitations remove v1's high-dimensional-dataset discussion and add the cost of doubling feature counts and alternative missingness encodings.

D1.justification: v1 promises future code release; v2 supplies a repository URL. Appendix A changes the OpenML benchmark identifier from 297 to 336, and Appendix L documents the MNAR generator's slope and bias choices. Reported computation changes from approximately 700,000 runs and 2.5 CPU years to approximately 1,000,000 runs and 325 CPU days for MCAR. The existing hyperparameter tables remain unchanged; these totals do not establish an efficiency gain.

R1.justification: v2 adds targeted references on imputation benchmarks, benchmark variance, MNAR generation, and missingness-aware modeling, including Bertsimas et al. (2024), Luengo et al. (2012), Pereira et al. (2024), Lenz et al. (2024), and NeuMiss. Rubin (1976) is removed. The overall positioning around quantifying when imputation helps prediction remains stable.

P1.justification: The introduction is rewritten to explain the controlled experimental factors more explicitly, and tuning and computation paragraphs are reorganized. v2 adds a dedicated MNAR subsection and an appendix contents page, while retaining most existing exposition and the main section sequence. Wording, headings, and publication-header text receive additional edits.

P2.justification: v2 adds nine figures covering missing-rate, feature-importance, indicator, and MNAR analyses. Existing slope plots gain significance symbols and legends, dataset panels are rearranged, and critical-difference diagrams are redistributed across pages. Runtime and scatterplot material is retained and renumbered from v1 Appendices G/H to v2 J/K. The document also adopts the ICLR layout.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens evidence for the paper's central conclusions. Questions supported largely by argument in v1—extension beyond MCAR and the source of indicator benefits—receive MNAR experiments and explicit controls, while statistical tests strengthen the central effect-size analysis. These gains outweigh reduced high-dimensional coverage and reporting defects, including Table 1's dataset mismatch and captions still claiming 20 datasets. The single tested MNAR mechanism nevertheless does not establish a universal MCAR upper bound.
